title: India Is Listing 'AI-Proof' Jobs and Sectors It Wants to Lead Globally, Goyal Says
excerpt: Speaking in Berlin, Piyush Goyal said the Commerce Ministry is identifying professions AI cannot replace — handicrafts and handloom among them — and sectors where India can take a global lead.
body:
• Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal, speaking in Berlin on October 23, said his ministry has begun identifying "AI-proof professions" — work where AI can add efficiency but cannot replace people.
  • He named handicrafts and handloom as work no amount of AI can replace, and handicrafts, handloom, culinary arts and tourism as sectors where India can take a global lead; he also called media itself AI-proof.
  • Goyal addressed Indian researchers and students in Germany — home to about 330,000 people of Indian origin and 60,000-70,000 Indian students — urging them to build careers linked to India's growth.
  • The exercise sits alongside the IndiaAI Mission's Rs 10,371.92 crore outlay for 20 indigenous foundation-model projects.

India's Commerce Ministry has begun identifying "AI-proof professions" as part of national workforce planning, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said in Berlin on Friday, arguing that the country should concentrate on work artificial intelligence can assist but never replace — and on sectors where India can lead the world.

"I got my Ministry to start working on what are the AI-proof professions. After all, we have to plan as a nation for so many millions of people," Goyal said, according to The Hindu. He cited handicrafts and handloom as examples: "No amount of AI can replace that." Asked how such sectors would be supported, he said incentives would be "a mix of several initiatives, some privately led, some government led, some people led, some opportunity led." Mint reported he also counted media among the AI-proof sectors, telling journalists: "Look at the media itself. You guys are also in an AI proof sector."

"I got my Ministry to start working on what are the AI-proof professions. After all, we have to plan as a nation for so many millions of people."

— Piyush Goyal, Commerce and Industry Minister

Pitching to the diaspora in Germany

Goyal was speaking during an official visit to Germany and the Netherlands, addressing Indian science and technology researchers and students. Germany hosts about 330,000 people of Indian origin and between 60,000 and 70,000 Indian students. Pressed on how India would persuade such talent to return, he said "it's not just about money; it's about the enabling environment, the support of the ecosystem." Mint reported the government will also write to embassies and high commissions to push Indian participation in global AI, startup and semiconductor conferences and fairs.

The policy backdrop

The professions exercise runs parallel to the IndiaAI Mission, which carries an outlay of Rs 10,371.92 crore and is backing 20 indigenous foundation-model projects, including Sarvam AI, Gnani.AI, BharatGen and Avataar AI. NITI Aayog warned last year that India's technology-services sector faces job-displacement risk by 2031, while estimating up to 4 million new jobs could be created in five years — the tension the ministry's list is meant to manage. The trade backdrop Goyal cited was strong: September merchandise exports rose 23% year on year to $44.4 billion, and the IMF has raised its FY2026-27 India GDP forecast by 60 basis points to 7%.

What to watch

No list or timeline has been published yet. The test will be whether the ministry's AI-proof map arrives with skilling, credit and export support attached for the named sectors — handicrafts, handloom, culinary arts and tourism — and whether it shapes the choices of the students and researchers Goyal was addressing, many of whom work in exactly the AI-exposed fields the list is designed to complement rather than replace.
nri_angle: The ministry's AI-proof list signals which India-facing skills and services sectors will get policy backing, relevant to diaspora professionals in AI-exposed roles and wellness and finance entrepreneurs.
author: Diaspora Desk

items: Handicrafts: No AI can replace this sector.
Handloom: Essential for preserving traditional skills.
Culinary Arts: Human creativity is irreplaceable.
Tourism: Personal touch is vital in this industry.
